translations.text: He himself set in place the sun and the moon, the stones and the earth, the stream out into the sea, water and cloud, through the might of his wonders.
The Measurer in his might holds the deep circuit all around in purity, and the whole world.
It seemed to them in their minds that it could be so: that they themselves would be lords of heaven, rulers of glory.
But they had to plunge into the deep surge, down beneath the headlands into the abyssal ground, greedy and ravenous. God alone knows how he had condemned that guilty host!
"It seemed to you alone that you had power over all, over heaven and earth, that you were holy God, the Creator himself. Now you are one of the wicked, bound fast in a fiery prison."
He gave off sparks of fire and venom when he began to speak; that is no fair joy when he drove out words in his torments:
"Dragons dwell forever at the door of hell, hot in their hearts; they cannot help us.
But I must at times, in flight and on the wing, seek out dwellings, and so must more of you who set in motion the beginning of this pride.

We need not expect that the King of glory will ever grant us a dwelling, a homeland as our possession, as he did before, eternal dominion; the Son of the Ruler has power over all, over glory and over torments.
Therefore I must wander the more widely, abject and wretched, tread the paths of exile, deprived of glory, cut off from blessings, possessing no joy up among the angels,
because I once said that I myself was lord of heaven, ruler of creatures. But it turned out worse for me!"
So the accursed spirit told in words all his hardships together, stained with crimes (a fiery gleam, mingled with venom, stood throughout that terrible cave):
"I may not enjoy a more hopeful home, cities or dwellings, nor may I ever again gaze with my eyes upon the bright creation.

Very often we, the children of the Saviour, brought the sound of glory to his bosom, where all of us around him, limbs around the beloved one, raised up the words of songs of praise and spoke them to the Lord.
O day of lights! O joy of God!
Alas that I am wholly bereft of eternal joy, that I cannot reach heaven with my hands, nor may I look up with my eyes, nor indeed shall I ever hear with my ears the voice of the brightest trumpet!
Now I am separated from the shining host, led away from the light into this hateful home.
I cannot conceive how I came into it, into this abyssal darkness, stained with wicked sins, cast out from the world.
I know now that he will be wholly bereft of eternal joys who does not think to obey the King of heaven, to please the Measurer.

I must endure this torment, woe and punishments and vengeance, deprived of good things, stained with deeds of old, because I thought to drive the Lord, the Ruler of hosts, from his seat; now, full of sorrowful care, I must set out on paths of exile, on wide journeys."
Then the adversary of God turned back to hell, when he had been humbled; so did his followers, greedy and ravenous, when God drove them into that hot dwelling whose name is hell.
Let us take as our joy the Lord of hosts, eternal happiness above, the Ruler of angels.
Let us bear in our breasts blithe thoughts, peace and wisdom; let us remember truth and right when we think to bow before the high throne and ask the Almighty for mercy.
Then he will not abandon us, but will give us life up among the angels, blessed joy.

The bright one shows us a secure home, bright city walls. Blessed souls, freed from sorrows, shine brightly there, where they may dwell forever after in the city and by the royal throne. Let us make that known!
As he himself said: "Righteous men, like the sun, beautifully adorned, will shine in their Father's kingdom, in the protected city."
Alas! The accursed one wrathfully resolved that he would not obey the King of heaven, the comforting Father.

That was a firm punishment; his thegns too had to dwell there in that terrible land, and never again hear the holy joy up in heaven, where they had often had a fair place in service, up among the angels.
They have nothing to hope for except cold and fire, woe and torments and a swarm of serpents, dragons and adders, and that dark home.
Then the Father of mankind will embrace them and bless them with his right hand, and lead them to the light, where they will have life forever and ever, a heavenly home, a bright city.
Then Satan, with dark thoughts, planned to build a high throne in heaven, up beside the Eternal One. He was their lord, the originator of evil.

Afterward he regretted it, when he had to sink down to hell, and his retinue with him, sliding into humiliation and the Saviour's hostility, and never afterward could they look upon the eternal face, world without end.
Then the Lord went down to hell by his might for the sake of the children of men; he wished to lead forth a great number of people, many thousands, up to their homeland.
Then came the sound of angels, a din at dawn; the Lord himself had overcome the fiend. The feud was still out in the open in the hours before dawn, when the terror came.
"Now I implore you, Guardian of the heavenly kingdom, by the household that you led here, the troops of angels, that I may be able and allowed to go up from here with my kin."
Oh, that was a fair thing, that the company came up to the homeland, and the Eternal One with them, the Lord of mankind, into the glorious city!

Then, by God's will, they had forty children, so that from them multitudes sprang up across the earth and were allowed to live for many winters, men in their homeland, until it happened again that the fiend drove them away once more through sins; he is hostile everywhere.
"In paradise I newly planted a tree with branches, so that its boughs bore apples high up, and you two ate the bright fruits, as the baleful one told you to, the servant of hell.
"I interceded for you when men pierced me on the cross, with spears on the gallows. The young man struck there, and I came back up to eternal joys, to the holy Lord."

[?] in the stronghold, and he commanded the all-bright angels to fetch the eleven disciples, and above all commanded them to tell Simon Peter that he might see God in Galilee, eternal and steadfast, as he had before.
Then the disciples all ran there, to where the Eternal One was.
They fell to the ground and bowed down at his feet; they thanked their Prince that it had so happened that they saw the Creator of the angels.
The living God had then set countless souls in their place. Then Judas was gone, he who had earlier sold the radiant one, the Lord Saviour, as [?];
That deed did him no good, when he sold the Son of the Ruler for a treasure of silver; the wretched monster paid him back darkly for it inside hell.
Now the Son sits at his Father's right hand; every day the Lord of hosts gives help and salvation to the children of men throughout the world.
It is known to many that he alone is the maker and ruler of all creatures through the power of his glory.
The holy angel [?] sits in the heavens, the Ruler with the prophets. The Son of glory has his own seat, enclosed by heaven.

He invites us there to the light through his healing, where we ourselves may sit with the Lord, up with the angels, and have that same light, where his holy household now dwells and lives in joys, where the splendour of glory is brightly revealed.
Let us take good thought that we eagerly obey the Saviour and please Christ. There is a more glorious life there than we could ever gain on earth.
The glorious Prince, almighty God, the Lord himself, has now appointed a meeting with us on Judgment Day.
He will command archangels with loud voices to blow trumpets over the dwellings of cities throughout the corners of the earth.
Then men will awaken out of this earth; the dead will arise from the dust through the Lord's might.
That will be the longest of days, and the greatest of din will be heard loudly, when the Saviour comes, when the Ruler travels with the clouds into this world.
He will then separate the beautiful and the unclean onto two sides, the good and the evil.
The righteous will ascend to rest with the Guardian of the heavens at his right hand.
Then those who may go into the city, into God's kingdom, will be joyful, and the King of all creatures will bless them with his right hand and call out over them all: "You are welcome!
Go into the light of glory, to the kingdom of heaven, where you will have eternal rest forever and ever."
Then the damned, those who sinned, will stand there, trembling over when the Son of God will judge them according to the sum of their deeds.

They expect that they may go to the glorious city, up to the angels, as others did. But the eternal Lord will speak to them; he said before all: "Go down now, you accursed ones, into the house of torment, in great haste. Now I do not know you."

Immediately after those words the accursed spirits, the captives of hell, will glide in throngs by the thousand and lead them there into that den of criminals, shove them to the bottom into that narrow torment,
and never afterwards may they ever come up from there, but there they must endure wretched punishment, fetters and prison, and suffer the cold deep abyss and the devil's talk:

how the black torment-slayers often cast it at them in reproach, how the fiends charge them with hostility and sin, in that they had often forgotten the noble Lord, the eternal sole Ruler, whom they should have had as their hope.
Come, let us consider, throughout this world, that we should begin to obey the Saviour!
Let us eagerly, through God's grace, keep in mind the glory of the spirit, how the blessed sit up there themselves in heaven, the sons of the Saviour!

There is a golden gate adorned with gems, wreathed with joys, for those who are allowed to go into the light of glory, into God's kingdom; and around the walls the spirits of angels and the blessed souls who journey from here shine beautifully.
There martyrs please the Creator and praise the High Father with holy voices, the King in the city.
They all say this: "You are the protector of men and heaven's judge, origin of angels, and you have led earth's offspring up to this blessed home."
So the thanes around their Prince praise the Guardian of glory with words. There is great majesty there and song at the throne; the King himself is there, Lord of all, in that eternal creation.
That is the Lord who suffered death for us, the Prince of angels.
Likewise he fasted forty days, the Creator of mankind, through the abundance of his mercies.
Then it befell the accursed one, who had earlier been cast out of the heavens so that he plunged into hell, when he tempted the King of all creatures.
He brought broad stones to his lap and told him to make loaves from them because of his hunger: "if you have so much power."

Then the eternal Lord answered him: "Did you think, accursed one, that it was not written: except me alone [?]... but you have established [?] ... the possessor of victory, light for the living, reward without end in the kingdom of heaven, holy joys."

Then the terrible one took him in his hands in mockery and lifted him onto his shoulders, the harmful spirit of evil [?], and climbed onto a mountain and set the Lord Saviour down on the hill: "Look now far and wide over the land-dwellers.

I will give you people and land to rule as you choose. Take from me here the city and the broad dwelling into your power, of the kingdom of the heavens [?], if you are the rightful king of angels and men, as you claimed before."
Then it seemed to him that from there to the door of hell was a hundred thousand miles by measure, as the Mighty One had commanded him to measure out the torment by his own skill.
Then he realised that he was standing on the bottom.
